observation.visible_scene: A wide view of a calm, dark lake under an overcast sky with a full rainbow arching overhead. A tree-lined shore runs across the middle distance, with a light-colored house and covered boat docks on the left and a small white canopy structure near the shoreline. A single person stands upright on a blue paddleboard in the open water, holding a paddle. Faint streaks (possible rain) appear on the water in some frames.
visible_changes: The paddleboarder translates leftward across the frame relative to the shore: their horizontal position moves from the right-of-center area toward the middle, closing the gap to the house/dock side (boarder-to-house separation shrinks markedly from first to last frame).
The background elements (house, docks, tree line) and the rainbow arc drift rightward within the frame over the clip, indicating a slow leftward camera pan that does not fully track the boarder.
Because the boarder moves left in the frame while the background moves right, the boarder's leftward motion relative to the shore is clear and persistent throughout the excerpt.
The boarder remains standing on the board with the paddle held at their side/raised in varying positions; no boarding, falling, or stopping is observed within the segment.
Water-surface ripple pattern and faint streak marks change subtly frame to frame, consistent with light disturbance, but no large wave or wake is visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the boarder was already paddling before t=0 or continues/changes direction after the last frame (the segment is a mid-action crop).
The cause or intent of the camera pan (handheld drift vs. deliberate tracking).
Whether the faint streaks are rain, spray, or lens artifacts.
uncertain_details: Exact paddle stroke timing and whether the boarder is actively paddling or being towed/drifting is not determinable from the frames.
The precise magnitude of camera pan versus boarder translation is approximate, based on relative pixel shifts of fixed shore features.
Small vertical streaks seen in a few frames may be rain or sensor noise rather than physical objects.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
